name: Lodhi
world_status: a description exists but is not accessible

earlier_scan.source_named: Dipankar Dasgupta 1978 (linguistic study covering Lodha; cited by Glottolog for subclassification), Anthropological Survey of India

sources.citation: Wikipedia, 'Lodhi language' (accessed 2026-09-17), citing Ethnologue 25 and LSI West Bengal Part I pp. 460-490.
sources.note: Phoneme inventory summarised from the LSI sketch (5 vowels, 4 diphthongs); nothing on stress. Notes the identity problem: 'both Munda and Indic varieties' may exist under the name Lodhi.

sources.citation: Language Division, Office of the Registrar General, India. 2021. Linguistic Survey of India – Orissa (27 sketches).
sources.note: No Lodha/Lodhi sketch in the volume; the only hit for 'Lodha' is the Dasgupta 1978 title in the Juang chapter bibliography. Nothing on Lodha stress.

sources.citation: Language Division, Office of the Registrar General, India. 2016. Linguistic Survey of India – West Bengal (Part I). Chapter "Lodha" by P. Edward Vedamanickam, pp. 458-494 (fieldwork Phulgeria village, Narayangarh block, Midnapore, Nov-Dec 2002).
sources.note: Silent on stress. The only suprasegmental remark (p. 462, heading 'Supra segmental Phonemes') is: 'The vowels become long in the word final position and that length is not phonemic in this language.' No mention of stress, accent, pitch or tone anywhere in the chapter (grep of the whole chapter text). Note: the chapter labels the language Munda and its data (pronouns im/am/ele/ani; numerals mon, ubar, uphe, iphon, moloy, tibru, tham, ghal) are Kharia, so it describes a Kharia lect of the Lodha/Kheria tribe rather than the Indo-Aryan lect Glottolog files as lodh1246.

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.x languoid page lodh1246 and reference page 46479 (Hammarström et al.).
sources.note: Classification Indo-European (Gaudian/Bengali-Assamese), based on Dasgupta 1978 pp. 152-153 ('close to Bengali not Munda'); alternative names Lodha, Lodi, Lohi, Lozi; only one descriptive reference (Dasgupta 1978, grammar sketch). Nothing on stress.

sources.citation: Dasgupta, Dipankar. 1978. "The Lodha Dialect of Midnapur." In Dipankar Dasgupta, Linguistic Studies in Juang, Kharia Thar, Lodha, Mal-Pahariya, Ghatoali Pahariya, pp. 151-176. Calcutta: Anthropological Survey of India, Government of India (xiii, 255 pp.).

sources.note: The only descriptive source Glottolog lists for lodh1246 and the basis of its Indo-Aryan classification; the volume is catalogued as 'chiefly phonology and morphology', so the 26-page Lodha chapter almost certainly has a phonology section and is the one place a first-hand stress statement for this lect could exist. HathiTrust search-only copies exist (mdp.39015024261037; uc1.b3177765); a library scan or a HathiTrust search-inside for 'stress' would settle it.
